To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) Scratch users are not all equally sophisticated programmers; 2) there is no significant relationship between level of participation and level of programming concepts used; 3) there is a small group of Scratch users that are highly engaged in the online community and use more complex programming; 4) girls and new users to the site tend to use less complex programming concepts.
the level of online participation is not related to the level of programming sophistication and that there is a group of highly engaged Scratch users who use the most advanced programming concepts.

there is a significant relationship between level of participation and level of programming complexity, but that the exception is a small group of high participation users who are also the most likely to use complex programming concepts, and that the groups of low participation users are primarily new users of the site or girls, who are also less likely to use more advanced programming concepts.
